Erin — great to meet you this morning. Thanks for the time and for walking through Acme's production translation pipeline and scale targets. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

Summary of needs
- Real-time translation endpoint (p95 latency target < 200ms for short-form requests)
- Peak throughput ~2k rps, steady-state ~600 rps
- Strong cost focus: want to understand per-1M token unit economics and how batching + caching can drive down spend
- Security/compliance: SOC2 + VPC/private deployment for PII workloads

Open questions we flagged
1) Typical sequence lengths and token distribution for your traffic (you mentioned median ~40 tokens, tail up to 512)
2) Expected cache hit rates for prefix reuse (any existing caching on your side?)
3) Acceptable model variants (open LLMs vs managed models) for quality vs cost tradeoffs

Proposed next steps
- Redwood/SE team to run a focused benchmark: 100k warm requests + simulated batching scenarios to estimate per-1M token costs under 3 cache hit assumptions (0%, 30%, 60%)
- We'll provide a cost comparison vs the hyperscalers (AWS Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic) with the same quality baselines and batching assumptions
- Schedule a 45-min bench review next week to walk the numbers and agree on an evaluation criteria set

I'll loop Marcus (SE) and Marissa (solutions) to draft the benchmark plan and cost worksheet. Marcus — can you prioritize a quick cost/TCO calc and an initial benchmark plan (attachment) for Erin? Erin/Tom — are you available Thu 3/19 or Mon 3/23 for the review?

Hi Erin / team — I put together an initial cost/TCO sketch and assumptions (see attached csv). High level summary below — these are back-of-envelope numbers to align expectations before we run the bench: 

Assumptions (benchmark baseline)- Model: 7B open LLM (quantized FP16-ish runtime) comparable quality to your current baseline- Median seq len: 40 tokens, Avg seq len for cost calc: 65 tokens (includes tail)- GPU: A100 equivalent for hyperscalers; Redwood uses optimized kernels and batching on similar hardware- Tokenization: cost quoted per model token; we normalize vendor units to model input+output tokens

Per-1M token estimated unit costs (USD)- Redwood (with typical auto-batching, no cache): $22 per 1M tokens- Redwood (with 30% cache hit): $16.5 per 1M tokens- Redwood (with 60% cache hit): $10.8 per 1M tokens- AWS Bedrock (managed open model, default settings): ~$35 per 1M tokens- OpenAI (gpt-4o-style managed): ~$60 per 1M tokens- Anthropic (Claude-like managed): ~$48 per 1M tokens

Notes on batching and latency tradeoffs
- We see diminishing latency returns when batching > 8 requests for short sequences; for your median 35–40 token requests, an effective batch size of 4–6 keeps p95 latency under 200ms while achieving most cost benefits.
- Redwood's KV/prefix caching reduces model computation linearly on cache hits (we charge only missing-token compute). So a 30% hit reduces compute cost ~30% on those requests — reflected in numbers above.

Recommended next technical tests
1) 100k warm-run with live traffic replay (your anonymized traces) to measure real cache-hit rates and latency at batch sizes 1/4/8
2) 1M token simulated run to validate per-1M cost extrapolations across vendors
3) Quality A/B on a representative 1k prompt set against your key languages to ensure open 7B model meets bar

I'll attach the redwood-vs-hyperscalers-cost-sheet.csv with line-item math and the benchmark plan (acme_benchmark_plan.xlsx). Aditya — happy to join the bench review on Mon 3/23 10:00 PT.
